messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Canary deployment 'release/2026-03-17' in eu-west-1 exceeded error rate threshold (12%). Triggered at 2026-03-17T16:22:01Z.

alex: paging @devon — canary rollout failing, high 5xxs and latency spike.

devon: on it. grabbing runbook (https://confluence/redwood/runbooks/canary-failures). which service?

maya: svc-inference-hosted, canary slice ~8% of traffic. I'm seeing 502/504 and sudden KV miss logs in the runtime.

charlie: tagging ops-sre for routing rollback if needed. @ops-sre any immediate blockers to flipping the flag?

devon: initial glance: error rate ~12% for canary group, stable ~0.2%. rollout started at 16:22. probable mismatch between model variant and cache warmup -> KV cache coherence failures. Recommend abort rollout, flip canary flag OFF, drain traffic, and fallback to stable model.

alex: agree. Maya, can you prep quick verification checks so we can confirm rollback success?

maya: prepping smoke script now. Will check /metrics/requests_by_model, /runtime/errors, and a sample inference smoke against stable.

devon: executing kill-switch command to abort rollout: 
```
# abort canary rollout
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/flags/rollout_abort \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"canary_2026_03_17","value":false}'
```

ops-sre: executed rollback flag flip at 16:24:05Z — API returned 200 OK. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by devon.

charlie: initiating traffic drain for canary slice to 0% using traffic-shift tool:
`rctl traffic shift --target canary --pct 0 --duration 60s`

emily: drain started (16:24:12Z). ETA ~40s. Monitoring health checks and ingress logs.

maya: quick metrics update (16:24:45Z): canary error_rate dropped to 1.1% (from 12%), p95 latency improving 120ms -> 98ms. Stable model error_rate steady at 0.25%.

devon: routing reverted to stable model v2.3.5 for all regions. Starting verification suite against top-3 impacted orgs.

alex: customer impact summary so far: three enterprise tenants saw elevated errors (~3 minutes), we routed them back to stable model automatically. CS notified and preparing outbound. No signing/key exposure.

charlie: running targeted smoke against tenant org-112, org-207, org-334:
`curl -s -H "X-Org: org-112" https://api.redwood/health/model | jq '.status'`

maya: org-112: OK, org-207: OK, org-334: OK (all within expected latency).

emily: leaving oncall note and will hand off monitoring to charlie in 30m. I'll post the incident stub and paged customers if needed.

devon: follow-ups: 1) pin model versions for rollouts so canary variant checks preflight, 2) add canary circuit breaker for KV mismatch, 3) add checksum preflight for model KV cache keys. Filing INF-452 with details.

alex: good. please include timeline and the curl/traffic commands in the postmortem.

charlie: I'll stay on monitoring until metrics stable for 15m and then close the thread. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

ops-sre: confirmed final metrics at 16:27:15Z: global error_rate back to baseline. Closing active remediation steps.
